page_content:
### Machine Coding Round

#### Problem Statement: 

Your organization has started a new tech blog with interesting tech stories and you’re responsible for designing and implementing an in-memory search engine, supporting the search functionality on the blog content. 

#### Requirements: 
* It should be possible to create a dataset in the search engine. 
* It should be possible to insert documents into a given dataset. Each document is simply a piece of text.
* It should be possible to search through documents for a search pattern in a given dataset. 
* It should be possible to order the search results
* Search Pattern: Initially search pattern would be sequence of words, but can be extensible for different search patterns:
    - Sequence of words containing words
    - Sequence of words containing words maintaining the order
    - Sequence of words containing words maintaining the order in sequence(substring)
- Ordering Logic: Initially ordering pattern would be latest published article, but can be extensible for different search patterns:
    - Ordering can be recently published articles
    - Ordering can be recently updated articles
    - Ordering can be recently searched articles
    - Ordering can be done based on Author.

#### Personal Feedback
- Interviewer wanted to get the O(1) fetch during query.
- Interviewer also wanted not to make too much memory consumption (during initial preprocessing of the blog content).
- The 30-40 minutes discussion went for Algorithmic/DSA related discussion on how to store/fetch the documents. 
- For effecient read/write queries discussion went around map, sorting, hashing, hash collisions, array manipulation, 2 Pointers, Trie implementatiton - which wasn't really scope of this interview. Is this normal?
- Got only 20 minutes for actual coding, probably didn’t do much to clear the round.
- The interviewer seemed very inexperience on how to navigate the interview.


Any hint on how to approach this problem?

title: Zepto | SDE 2 | Bengaluru | September 2024  [Offer]
page_content:
I appeared for interviews in Zepto for SDE 2 position in August 2024. The interviews were based on DSA and LLD. Find the details below. 

**Source :** Recruiter reached out to me on phone call via Instahyre.

There were total of 4 rounds. 

**Round 1 : (DSA) ->** Got two questions. Follow up questions were asked, emphasis was on TC and SC. 

* Q1 : [https://leetcode.com/problems/best-time-to-buy-and-sell-stock-ii/description/](http://) 

* Q2 : [https://leetcode.com/problems/rotting-oranges/description/](http://)

I was able to solve both these quetions as they were pretty much standard leetcode questions. I jumped to the optimal solution and skipped the brute force approaches. Interviewer was satisfied and gave good feedback at the end of interview. 

**Round 2 : (LLD) ->** Interviewer asked one question on LLD, then some authentication concepts, then design patterns. 

Q1 :  Design a system for managing customer orders and deliveries in a quick commerce platform. 

*  How would you structure the system to manage customer orders, inventory, and deliveries?
* How would you design a system to handle order prioritization for fast delivery, especially during peak times?
* How would you handle different payment methods such as credit cards, digital wallets, and cash on delivery?

I gave the DB design first. After the interviewer agreed with the Schema, was asked to write APIs on adding products to cart and placing orders. Interviewer asked to handle edge cases and write proper error handling scenarios. Further we discussed order prioritization and other things mentioned in the above question for next 5 mins. 

Q2 : How authentication can be done in the above two APIs. 

Suggested JWT tokens here. Was asked what are JWT tokens are how they work as follow up questions. 

Q3 : What kind of design patterns can be used here ? 

I suggested Factory Pattern, Builder Patterns and Strategy Pattern for several features of the app. Interviewer deep dived into Factory Pattern. I suggested to use factory pattern for handling payments from different sources (point 3 from Q). Further I was asked to inmplement the Processors, Factory and exmaple usage for payments. I used Java and wrote implementations for Credit card payments (others were skipped) and then wrote a factory class to generate objects based on payment methods chosen by user. Also wrote a small code to use this. 

Interviewer was satisfied. Interview lasted for 1 hr 15 mins. 

**Round 3 : (HM) ->** One LLD question, One DSA, previous project discussion and Some behaviourial questions. 

Q1 -> Design a app like Google Calendar. 

* Users should be able to create meetings.
* Users can schedule events/meetings with a title, description, start/end time, location, and participants.
* Users can add participants to meetings and notify them.
* The system should send notifications for upcoming meetings.
* Users should be able to accept/decline invitations.

I was asked the DB design only. I made entities, columns and relationships to cover all the features asked above.  Interviewer suggested to add more entities to add decoupling. Then asked how will you seperate a shared calendar and personal calendar for every user. I suggested adding few more columns in every event entity to identify the event as personal or shared event. Also added permissions section to allow shared events to be for View only or View/Edit access. Dicussion went on for 20 -25 mins. Interviewer seemed satisfied with my solution. Coding was skipped.

Q2 : Insert new nodes into a CLL in such a way that they always remain in sorted state. 

Gave an O(n) optimal solution. Skipped brute force approach.

Interviewer seemed satisified and moved ahead. 

Q3 : Interviewer asked what was your favourite features that you implemented in your previous orgs. Also asked how do you handle conficts in work and handle work pressure in tight deadlines. 

I shared answers from my experience. 

**Round 4 : (HR) ->** This round lasted for 20 mins and the HR mostly talked about the working culture at Zepto and took any questions I had in the end. 

**Results :** Selected. I got the call next day about the offer.

**Compensation :** https://leetcode.com/discuss/compensation/5796402/Zepto-or-SDE-2-or-Bengaluru

About 1.5 weeks later, another HR representative called to discuss compensation. I told them that I already had an offer and requested that Myntra's offer at least match it. title: How a Company Took My Future and Left Me Feeling Lost and Defeated
page_content:
A company destroyed everything I worked so hard for, and now I feel completely lost. I'm always tense and worried, with a constant pain in my chest that I can't shake. Every day feels like a battle, and I don’t know how to get out of this stress and struggle.

I come from one of the top NITs, where I poured my heart into preparing for JEE, dreaming of becoming a software engineer and working with a great company. Every day, I dedicated myself to solving DSA problems, balancing academics, and preparing for placements. My dreams were centered on building a successful career, but now, everything feels uncertain and fragile.

In 2023, the internship season started at our college, and my friends and I were applying to various companies.

In our college, there is a rule that all undergraduate students have to undergo an internship or vocational training for a minimum period of 15 days. There is also 1 credit for the internship, so we are required to complete one.

I registered for many companies. The companies in our college do not visit in decreasing order of CTC, it's quite random. I was shortlisted for a renowned consultancy company, and I couldn't back out because of this rule in our college: "Any student who is shortlisted for one placement process is required to go through the entire selection process unless rejected by the company. Any student who withdraws deliberately in the midst of the selection process will be disallowed from placement for the rest of the academic year. Students must maintain discipline and demonstrate ethical behavior throughout the placement process. Any student found violating discipline or defaming the institute's name will be disallowed from placements for the rest of the academic year."

I interviewed with the company, and my resume included a few of my C++ and MERN stack development projects. I was asked about web development basics and CS fundamentals. I also told them I was interested in software development and wanted to work for a software company. The company did not mention any details regarding a PPO or CTC, the interview was for an internship. On the other hand, companies offering PPOs usually disclose their CTC (if PPO) along with the internship stipend.

So, I was selected for the internship, and while preparing for my on-campus placement for 2024, I continued solving DSA problems and focusing heavily on academics.

I interned at the renowned consulting company this summer.

During onboarding, we were told that the internship would give us a sense of the company's work culture and environment. We were assured that after the internship, we could decide whether we wanted to express interest in a full-time position.

I was happy about having the option to express interest after working for two months.

Unfortunately, I was assigned to the Data Analytics department instead of Application Technology, Business Transformation, or any other department with more software work. This department had more data analytics work and less development. I was disappointed and requested my People Manager to assign me something related to development for the internship.

I worked there but felt it wasn't the place I wanted to work. There was no intellectually intensive software work, and no emphasis on design patterns for software development. I wanted to opt out of the PPO.

I reached out to a senior from the 2023 batch through LinkedIn who interned at this company, as they didn’t visit for internships for the 2024 batch. The senior reassured me that the company shares a PPO form, and we could opt out of the PPO, which would only be given to students who expressed interest. I was not aware of the CTC at that time, so I was curious to know the details.

I contacted the HR responsible for these matters through MS Teams. He first asked about my campus, as this company offers CTCs based on the campus you are from, which vary. He informed me of the CTC they offer to our college students, and it was very low considering market standards. I asked if we could opt out of the PPO, and he confirmed we could, without any issues. He told me I could drop a mail to opt out.

A few days later, the PPO evaluation form was released, and I marked "No" on the form. I informed the HR that I had received the form and marked "No" as I didn't want a PPO. I also asked if we needed to do anything else, such as dropping a mail. He told me that filling out the form was sufficient, and I wouldn’t need to do anything else, I would not be offered a PPO.

I informed my team that I wasn’t interested in a PPO, and they were very supportive, wishing me well for my future and the upcoming placement season.

The placement season began, and by this time, I had achieved a CGPA above 9 in our Computer Science and Engineering Department. I had also solved many DSA problems, mostly on LeetCode, and participated in several contests on competitive programming platforms like Codeforces. So, I had become a decent competitive programmer with good knowledge of CS fundamentals and had also learned the basics of system design.

I was sure I wouldn’t receive a PPO, so I didn’t apply to several renowned companies like ZS, Amdocs, and Sigmoid. In our college, companies don’t visit in decreasing order of CTC, and I was focused on my DSA studies and CS fundamentals for placements, hoping to work for a software company and make an impact.

At that time, I was preparing for the Oracle interview, which would soon be held on campus. Oracle came for two roles this year. I was preparing specifically for the company and dreamed of working on scalable products and making an impact by building them.

Then, suddenly, the company where I had interned released a list of students for PPOs. I was certain my name wouldn’t be on it, as I had opted out and was assured I wouldn’t receive one. To my surprise, my name was on the list. I was very anxious, as I had made many sacrifices by opting out. I called the HR and told him that despite marking "No," my name was still on the list. He told me there was no issue, and I could inform the Training and Placement Cell to not send my name to the company, and there would be no problem. Another student also called the HR, who was rude to him, saying he knew the placement rules of our college and that because he marked "No," that was why he was offered a PPO. The HR was not helpful at all and was rude to everyone.

I informed the Training and Placement Cell, and they told me I was bound to accept the PPO because of this rule: "All students who will be offered a PPO are bound to accept the offer, and hence all recruitment or placement-related activities will be frozen for that student." I had no other option, and the company forced us into this. I felt helpless and hopeless. All my dreams were shattered, and I felt like the world was against me. I had nothing left, and I was constantly thinking about it, feeling tense, with chest pain. I became completely demotivated and unable to focus on academics or anything else.

These companies can do whatever they want, and they can play with students' lives. Students have no voice. I have many proofs, including conversations where the HR assured me I wouldn’t be offered a PPO if I mark "No" in the PPO evaluation form.

Why did they tell us we could decide whether to opt for a PPO after the internship? And why did they even ask for our opinion through a Google form for PPO evaluation if our opinion didn’t matter? This is intolerable. How can they do this? I am very worried and nervous.

Now, it feels like my entire life has shattered in front of me. Every dream I had, every late night spent grinding through DSA problems, every single sacrifice I made just to get to this point, none of it seems to matter anymore. I worked so hard to get into a good college, to become the software engineer I always dreamt of being, and now it feels like all my hard work has been for nothing. The sleepless nights, the pressure to maintain a high CGPA, the constant struggle to balance competitive programming with academics—all of it feels worthless.

This experience has left me devastated. I feel like I’ve been betrayed by the very system that was supposed to help me build my future. After being reassured I wouldn’t receive the PPO, they still forced it on me, destroying my chance to apply to other companies, companies I had been preparing for with everything I had. I feel utterly helpless, and no matter how hard I try, I can't escape this overwhelming sense of defeat. My chest tightens with anxiety every day, and it feels like there’s no way out.

I don’t know what to do anymore. It’s like the world has turned its back on me, and I’m trapped in a situation I never wanted, with no options left. Everything I worked so hard for is slipping away, and I don’t know how to stop it. I’ve lost my motivation, my drive, and I’m scared of what’s next.

I'm at a point where I need help more than ever. If anyone can offer guidance or show me a way forward, I would be incredibly grateful. I’ve worked so hard to get to where I am, but right now, I feel lost and unsure of how to rebuild. It's not easy for me to admit, but I'm struggling to believe in myself, and finding a lifeline would mean the world to me.

[Link to the OA question](https://leetcode.com/discuss/interview-question/5382948/Wayfair-or-SWE-or-OA)

I had seen this problem before, which helped me complete it successfully with all follow-ups. Without prior exposure, I don't think I would have been able to finish it on time.

**Low-Level Design (LLD) Round**
The problem was [bike rental shop question](https://leetcode.com/discuss/interview-question/4503513/Wayfair-or-L2-L4-or-Virual-Onsite-or-LLD-or-Bike-Rental-Shop), and I was well-prepared. However, the interview was a bit chaotic. The interviewer was new (conducting their first interview), and a more senior member was shadowing. Unfortunately, the senior member interrupted frequently, creating confusion as they seemed to have different expectations. It felt like I was interviewing with two people who weren't on the same page, which affected my performance.
Make sure to cover key areas like API design, class structure, and database schema.

**High-Level Design (HLD) Round**
The problem was a [mobile check-in system](https://leetcode.com/discuss/interview-question/system-design/5784840/Wayfair-or-L3-or-HLD-or-August-2024). I struggled with time management and was only able to cover the basic components and requirements.
In an HLD interview, try to touch on as many topics as possible: rate limiting, caching, asynchronous processing, normalization, consistent hashing, LRU cache, analytics, etc.

**Verdict**: Rejected
**Feedback**: While I performed well in the coding round, my performance in LLD and HLD was not up to the expectations. Had I done better in any one of these design rounds, I could have cleared the interview.

The next day(on 16th February), I got a call from HR that I had cleared the Online Assessment and that my Interview was scheduled after 4 days on 20th February at 2 PM.

It was a Zoom call that lasted for over 60 minutes.
There were two interviews.
They were friendly.
They made me feel comfortable.
First, they asked me to introduce myself.
Then they jumped over to SQL queries.
They asked me 9-10 SQL queries.
I was prepared for it and hence I was able to write the SQL queries correctly for almost all the questions.
The interviewers were satisfied with it.
Then they asked me a question on C programming.
They gave me a piece of code void func(){ int arr[10];}
They told me that this function is being called recursively infinite number of times and I have a memory of 2 Mega Bytes.
Then he asked me if this would give an error if it would keep on running infinite times or if my system would crash.
I was able to answer this question and the interviewer was also satisfied with it.
Then they asked me the difference between “call by value” and “call by reference” and asked me to explain it using an example.
Then they asked me a medium-level DSA question for which I was able to provide the logic and wrote the pseudo-code for the same.
The interviewers were happy with my approach. In the end, they asked me if I had any questions and the interview ended.

**Round-3 (HR Round)**
I got a call from HR the very next day(on 21st February) that I got a positive response from the panel and I had my HR Round Scheduled on 22nd Feb.

I read all the past interview experiences of the HR round of Morgan Stanley.
I read about the company and the core values of the company.
I also prepared for some behavioural questions.
It was again a Zoom call.
The interviewer joined late and straightaway asked me to introduce myself.
Then he asked me about the project that I had mentioned in my resume.
He asked why had used MongoDB over SQL database.
Then he asked me some behavioural questions:

What are your aspirations and career plans?
Why do you want to join Morgan Stanley?
What do you know about the business side of Morgan Stanley?
Core values of Morgan Stanley?
There are two teams, one working on Python and the other working on C++, which team you prefer to join and why?
Give a scenario where you had to sacrifice your ethics.
Tell an interesting incident related to your project.
Given a scenario where you are working on a team and you have to deliver a product in one month’s deadline to a client but some bugs in the project hypothetically can’t be removed in one month, you have two options – either to deliver the product late or to deliver a product full of bugs, what will you do?
The interview lasted for about 30 minutes. The interviewer asked me if I had any questions and it ended.

After exactly 3 weeks, I received an email that I had been shortlisted for the Summer Analyst role at Morgan Stanley for the Summer of 2024.

title: 22 Interviews, Countless Rejections, and Finally: Confluent
page_content:
The last few months have been nothing short of challenging. I hadn't received my salary for the last four months and after that I was laid off.This was an incredibly tough phase, both financially and emotionally. 

I started applying for jobs regularly in early July, and the first company I interviewed at was ([**BharatX**](https://leetcode.com/discuss/interview-experience/5753820/BharatX-or-Backend-Engineer-or-Bengaluru-or-JULY-2024-(GHOSTED))). There were two rounds:
1. **Project discussions**
2. **Machine coding round**

Both rounds happened within a span of 7 days, and they went really well. I was hopeful about hearing something positive, but unfortunately, I never got a response. Despite my efforts to follow up via calls and emails, I received no reply.

# The Rejections Pile Up
I kept applying to multiple companies, and I got calls from notable ones like **Nutanix, Cred, HackerRank, FiMoney, Chalo, Swiggy, Uber, Meesho and Flexport**, but couldn't progress past the test/screening stages. 

Next, I interviewed at **[Cloudera (link for exp)](https://leetcode.com/discuss/interview-experience/5754031/Cloudera-or-Software-Engineer-(Golang)-or-JULY-2024-or-(ON-HOLD))**, my first opportunity with a big company. My first round was perfect — I answered everything about DSA, projects, internal workings of HashMap/Sets, hashing, and Linux. I felt confident when I received a call for the second round.

In the second and final round, which was with the hiring manager, I was expecting a mix of technical and HR questions, but it turned out to be entirely technical. We talked about the team I would potentially be joining.

After such a positive experience, I was eagerly waiting for a selection. However, despite my follow-ups, the HR kept delaying the result.

# More Interviews, More Hope, and More Waiting
Around the same time, I received a referral for **[Razorpay (link for exp.)](https://leetcode.com/discuss/interview-experience/5754727/Razorpay-or-Software-Engineer-or-Bengaluru-or-August-2024-or-Rejected)**. There were two rounds:
1. **Low-Level Design (LLD)**
2. **Hiring Manager Round**

I was hopeful for good news, but after multiple follow-ups, I was informed that I was rejected. This hit me hard. After giving what I felt were great interviews at both **Cloudera** and **Razorpay**, I couldn't figure out what went wrong.

I also had a two-hour LLD interview at **[Allen Digital (link for exp)](https://leetcode.com/discuss/interview-experience/5758924/Allen-Digital-(Recro)-or-Software-Engineer-or-Bengaluru-or-Rejected)**, which didn’t go as well, especially in terms of database design, and I was rejected.

Then I gave 2 interviews at **[PICE](https://leetcode.com/discuss/interview-question/5759045/PICE-or-Backend-Engineer-or-Bengaluru-or-August-2024-or-Rejected)**, a fintech startup in Bangalore.
Everything went pretty good in both the rounds, but I still got the rejection without any feedback. I kept asking myself what did I do wrong.

# The Turning Point
Despite the rejections, I kept learning and applying. I then received calls from **Confluent**, **Zomato**, and **Zepto** — three amazing opportunities.

I gave:
- **3 technical rounds** at **Confluent**
- **1 interview** at **Zomato**
- **3 technical rounds** at **Zepto**

Finally, after a Culture Fit round at **Confluent**, I received the call I had been waiting for — **I was selected**! 
After few days, I received an offer from **Zepto** as well, but I decided to join **Confluent**. I also chose to withdraw from the process at **Zomato**, as my mind was already set.

# Lessons Learned: Trust the Process
After being approached by more than 20 companies and giving over 22 rounds of interviews, here's my biggest takeaway: **Things will happen when they are meant to happen**. No matter how hard we try, if something is meant for us, it will come to us at the right time.

That doesn’t mean we stop trying. In fact, the only thing we can control is our effort — giving our best is all we can do from our side. We need to believe in ourselves and our skills.

If you're good enough, good things will come your way. All you need is a little time, persistence, and faith in yourself.

PS - You can find my other posts here - [**Zomato**](https://leetcode.com/discuss/interview-experience/5763557/Zomato-or-Software-Engineer-or-Gurgaon-or-Sept-2024), **[Zepto](https://leetcode.com/discuss/interview-experience/5763474/Zepto-or-Software-Engineer-or-Bengaluru-or-September-2024-or-Offer)**, **[Confluent](https://leetcode.com/discuss/compensation/5754364/Confluent-or-Software-Engineer-or-Remote)**

title: 6 months+ Interview Prep Journey [Laid Off]
page_content:
Education: B.Tech NIT

Prior Experience: MNC. Impacted by Layoff (> 6 months)

Was Impacted by Layoffs in First week of March. Took > 6 Months to land offers. Sharing Month wise preparation and interview experiences.

**March-April** **(*The initial burst of Motivation*)**

The news came as a shock to me and took couple of days to even register what actually happened. Started doing LC on a daily basis with occasional Design questions(HLD).
Started applying from 2nd/3rd week of march, got a couple of calls but couldnt make it past the initial stages.
Was still very confident to close out the job hunt in 6-8 weeks.

**Phonepe**: https://leetcode.com/discuss/interview-experience/5058789/phonepe-sde2-bangalore-55yoe [Reject]
Interviewed for **Arista Networks** but there were a lot of questions around Netwokring, hence couldnt clear it.[Reject]
Appeared for OA of **New Relic**, cleared the test and was asked to travel to a different city for in person interviews. Sadly i was going home at that time for Holi and asked the recruiter if its possible to reschedule it to next week to which she agreed. But tried reaching out to her multiple times the following week and didnt get any response.

Wasnt getting as many calls from recruiters as i expected earlier. Since i had very recently switched to the last company, my profile was not even getting shortlisted due to frequent job changes.

Started to lose confidence because of lack of responses.

**May (*The Ghosting Phase*)**

Thats when i started to feel a bit(more) anxious. Till now only a couple of people around me knew about my job status as was too embarrassed to share it with my friends/family.

Started to get some responses from companies. Recruiter screens were getting scheduled but when i joined, no one attended the meeting. Inspite of Multiple followups on mails and on calls, didnt get a single response back from them.
**OCI** scheduled a recruiter pre screen and never showed up.

**Microsoft** Recruiter reached out for a hiring drive, got my availability, didnt get any invite. Tried reaching out to the recruiter and via some friends internally as well, was updated that the interview will be scheduled the following week, nothing happened again.
This happened 2-3 times and eventually i never got any invite for the interview.

Was paralelly appearing for whatever Online Assessments i was getting from Microsoft or any other companies but even after clearing the tests, i wasnt getting any responses.

By the Second week of May, started to maintain streaks on daily questions on Leetcode and was more motivated than ever.

Dont remember if i gave any substantial interviews during this period.

**June (*The month of Realization*)**

Kept on maintaining the streaks till June Mid.

Gave a few interviews:
**Microsoft**:  https://leetcode.com/discuss/interview-experience/5338820/microsoft-hiring-drive-june-7-bangalore [Reject]
Never got any update from the recruiter. All i ever got was "***We are still waiting for the feedback***" for months.

But still nothing seemed to be working out. Either i was somehow being put up with some unrealistic hard questions in interviews or i just messed up big time.

Again got Ghosted by couple of Companies.

1. **Coackroach Labs** recruiter sync was scheduled, was recheduled multiple times but the recruiter never showed up.
2. Was shortlisted for **Zepto** drive and some other companies, never received any invites.
3. Cleared Online assessment for **Salesforce**, got the call from recruiter for an in person interview in bangalore in next couple of days but sadly i was in my hometown at that time. Requested to have the interview a few days later as it wasnt possible to travel back, but got no response even after multiple followups.

I am no expert on the definition of depression but i didnt have anything to look forward to for the next day, started being in my own shell, didnt feel like sleeping at nights  since didnt want to face another day of applying for jobs and getting rejection mails. Stopped caring about myself, stopped talking to people, stopped enjoying anything and everything around me. Lost track of what day of the week it is. Thought about going to therapy multiple times but being jobless for months didnt go well with my finances so i guess it just felt like a waste of money.

Towards mid of June took some mental break, went on a solo trip, spent some time with family (pretending to work infront of them).

**July** (***Mixed***)

Had sever mental breakdowns towards end of June and first week of July.
First couple of weeks were spent in trying to analyze whats going wrong and where can i improve myself. Was seeing people around me getting jobs in 4-6 weeks after starting to apply for jobs which again made me lose my confidence even more and question myself.

*Still kept on lying to my friends' questions "How's work going?" with a smile on my face.*

Again appeared for Microsoft interviews in an attempt to clear it this time, sadly, it was worse than last time. Got rejected after first round itself.
**Microsoft** : https://leetcode.com/discuss/interview-experience/5465329/microsoft-sde2-bengaluru-drive-10-july [Reject]

By the 3rd week of July, started getting a few calls from recruiters and had a few initial syncups, exploratory, tech screen rounds.
Stepped up on the preparation even more.

**August-Sept** (Well, Finally!!!)

Gave up on everything (sleep, workout, hanging out with friends, movies, deactivated Instagram, limited my Phone screen time). Was feeling mentally and physically exhausted on a daily basis with just a few hours of sleep.
Fortunately, i had started to plan every day hour wise in order to accomodate interview schedules. Started giving 10+ interviews on a weekly basis and drives on the weekends (appeared for even more than 17 rounds of interviews a few weeks)

Things started to happen at OCI. Yes there were some places where i could have done better but was still looking forward to an offer as overall the interviews went good. But sadly received rejection. This took a heavy toll on me but just somehow pushed myself to not crib about it prepare for the other upcoming interviews.

**Microsoft** - Cleared initial OA and first 3 rounds, things messed up in the Hiring Manager round. [Reject]
Ghosted by **ServiceNow** and **PayPal**

Other Interview experiences during this period(Aug-Sept)-

**Wayfair**: https://leetcode.com/discuss/interview-experience/5756032/Wayfair-or-L3-or-Bangalore-or-Offer
**Adyen**: https://leetcode.com/discuss/interview-experience/5757749/Adyen-or-Java-Backend-or-Bangalore-or-Reject [Reject]
**Atlassian**: https://leetcode.com/discuss/interview-experience/5758945/Atlassian-or-P40-or-Offer-or-6-Years
**Spare**: https://leetcode.com/discuss/interview-experience/5757709/Spare-or-Backend-Developer-or-6-Years-or-Reject [Reject]
**Goldman Sachs**: https://leetcode.com/discuss/interview-experience/5756181/Goldman-Sachs-or-VP-or-Bangalore-or-Offer-or-6-Years
**Salesforce**: https://leetcode.com/discuss/interview-experience/5757562/Salesforce-or-SMTS-or-Offer-or-6-YOE

**UIPath**: Rejected after second round [Reject]
**Allen**: Rejected after Round 2 [Reject]

Got the first offer from Wayfair but somehow just wanted to get something better considering the negative reviews around the company.
Eventually in the last week of August and first week of september got Offers from *Atlassian, Goldman Sachs and Salesforce* as well.

***Purpose of this Post?*** : Someone out there might be in the same boat as me and might be losing hope as i did multiple times. And a reminder to self as well to not lose hope.
***My suggestion?*** : Keep pushing! Eventually things will fall into place and your hard work will payoff. You will get what you deserve. Sometimes all you can do is keep working hard and do the hardest possible thing: **WAIT!** 
To the jobs I applied in march/April, i was getting responses in July. I hate to say this but sometmes, yes luck can definitely be a big factor when it comes to job hunt. 
Life is uncertain and more often than not things wont go even remotely close to how you planned them out. I had a lot of plans financially this year, everything just went down the drain. But this wont stop me from dreaming big and planning for my future.

***What kept me going through this period?*** : Guess i am someone who tries to find something positive out of every situation. Always thought *"I am gonna smile with a sense of pride when i make it past this phase and look back at it"*. Always thought about how this phase would make me a better person and how this would make me mentally stronger than ever.
Had weeks where i didnt have anything to look forward to, no interviews, no responses, so just kept pushing myself in the GYM. That sense of progress towards the end of every week in the gym did give me some relief.
Resorted to journaling, reading non-fictional books to keep myself sane through this period.
I am not an exceptional coder/developer. So tried working on my basics, even if i couldnt solve LC hard questions, kept on solving the medium/easy ones multiple times.

At this point, the interview was going badly for me. Then, they shifted to **SDLC** (Software Development Life Cycle) questions, asking me to explain **what SDLC is** and to describe the **Waterfall model**. They also asked **what documents are created after each step**. This led to questions about **testing**—they wanted to know the **different types of testing** and specifically asked about **User Acceptance Testing (UAT)**. They then asked, **"Is maintenance part of SDLC?"** and wanted me to explain **Agile** and how it works, along with details on **Scrum**.

The problem statement in the image describes a task related to analyzing and optimizing a log file. Here's a summary of the problem:A log file contains a series of entries represented by a permutation of length n integers. To analyze the log efficiently, n operations, indexed from 0 to n-1, are available. Each operation involves swapping two entries in the log.The goal is to select some of these n operations and apply them in any order to the log entries to produce the lexicographically smallest permutation, facilitating a more streamlined log analysis.The task is to return this lexicographically smallest permutation of entries.Additional notes provided in the problem statement include:
• Each operation can be used at most once.
• 0-based indexing is considered.
• A permutation is an array consisting of distinct integers from 1 to n in arbitrary order.
• The permutation p of length n is lexicographically less than the permutation q of length n if there is an index i such that for all j from 0 to i-2, the condition p[j] = q[j] is satisfied, and p[i] < q[i].
The problem also includes an example demonstrating the application of operations to achieve the optimal (lexicographically smallest) permutation for a given set of entries.

Example

entries [5, 4, 1, 3, 2]

Apply operation 2 to swap entries [1] and entries[2] to get entries [5, 1, 4, 3, 2].

Apply operation 1 to swap entries(0) and entries[1] to get entries [1, 5,4,3,2].

Apply operation 3 to swap entries[2] and entries[3] to get entries [1,5,2,4,3,]

Apply operation 2 to swap entries [1] and entries[2] to get entries=[4, 1, 3, 2]

Apply operation to swap entries[0] to get entries = [1,4,3,2]

1 ≤ entries[i] < n

title: Stripe | SDE2 | Aug 2024 | Horrible experience
page_content:
Had a nightmare experience interviewing at Stripe India office for a SDE2 role.

The recruiter sent an email enquiring whether I was interested in a role at Stripe. I sent back an affirmative email.
The recruiter emailed with a goodtime calendar to book a slot to "talk", I booked one for the same day in the evening. One would think it is with the HR to discuss the role, comp, etc? But no, it was with the engineering manager of the team. I'm completely unprepared at this point but somehow manage to get through this convo where I'm being grilled on my resume and role expectations. The manager is saying some things around work culture and expectations that are making me wary of the WLB to be expected and I'm wondering if it is a toxic work culture.

However, the feedback from the round is positive and the next round is setup, a coding round. They are using HackerRank as a platform and tbf I liked the interview question, it was setup as asking a simple question then adding more requirements as it progressed, the first problem was to make something like a map class, with a few modifications, so I built a wrapper class around it. The second part was using this wrapper to solve a simple problem and extend some functionality, this again was a breeze and we were around 15 mins into the interview so I was feeling pretty confident. The third (and last, as mentioned by the interviewer) wasn't really any modification to the logic or algo of the solution, but a taking the input in a specified format. Now, admittedly, I haven't practised String parsing a ton given the usual leetcode setup I'm used to, so I gravitate to regex, spend a few mins trying and failing to create a regex string, and then just do it through splitting the input strings into tokens and explicity checking logic in if else conditions. I finish the code and get it running with all the test cases passing with 10 mins to spare in the interview. At this point, I'm feeling very confident, but get met with radio silence from the recruiter, 2 weeks later, I reach out and the recruiter sets up a short call. She tells me that the feedback is a very weak hire, cue shocked pikachu face, I ask what the feedback was as my read of the interview was very good. The recruiter tells me that the interviewer noted I "seemed to not know how Strings work in Java" and "wasted time trying the wrong approach". I discussed the feedback a little more and she said that the interviewer also wanted me to go through with the regex approach and not abandon it. She says that they'll consider setting up another round, which is essentially a low level design round before doing more rounds as a "test". I'm a bit hesitant at this point, but feel that let's just go ahead and see what happens. 

This round was the worst interview of my life by a mile and then some. The interviewer showed up and spent the first fifteen minutes making me setup a repo for stripe interviews. Could this not have been informed before in a mail? I'm sitting staring at the interviewer while the brew command installs dependencies. I ask the interviewer if we can start in the meantime, and he says let's finish the setup first. Then, the interviewer asks me to go to Hackerrank. I ask what about the repo we just setup? and he informs me that the repo is required for the further interviews (remember the ones that I don't have scheduled). So, I've wasted 15 mins of an interview setting things up for a potential future interview. I navigate to HackerRank, where he gives me some requirements to create a "subscription tracking service" with a few test cases. I start coding on HackerRank, and the way the question is structured I spend the next 20 minutes writitng up a metric f\*\*k ton of data classes to model all of the various entities. I seem to have addressed the problem. Except I run into an issue, there is some problem with the static scope in declaration of one the data classes. So, I'm trying to figure that out and seeing me struggling this amazing interviewer (who has been sittting silently and not acknowledging me as I explain through the entire code flow, while keeping his cam off every few mins to savour his lunch) decides that now 47 mins into the interview where he had already wasted 15 mins, is the best time to say, "Btw, you're running out of time". I ask whether he sees what the issue is, he doesn't respond. I say, "I'm struggling with what seems to be a syntax issue, can I walk you through the code to explain my approach?", he says, "We want to run the code, please keep working on it".

At this point, 51 mins into the interview I stop sharing my screen and tell him that "we can close the interview, I can't figure it out". He asks me whether I have any questions for him and I reply, "None" and drop off the call. 

I have interviewed at a bunch of places, I have bombed interviews and been rejected with or without feedback. Never have I been treated with such unprofessionalism and callousness or felt so humiliated. Is this how the industry operates now?

title: Fresher : Data Scientist @MiQ | Interview Experience
page_content:
I had an on-campus interview with a company named MiQ (Media Intelligence Quotient).
The initial assessment rounds were online. There were 2 rounds.

## INITIAL ELIMINATION ROUNDS :
**- Round 1 : Hackerrank :**
*  2 DSA (1 Easy + 1 Medium )
*  4 SQL query (2 Easy + 1 Medium + 1 Hard)
*  10 to 15 MCQs on basic ML concepts, Aptitude etc.

There was a limited time constraint for this first round.
Most eliminations occured in this round itself.

**- Round 2 : PrespectAI :**
* Math based Games
* GMAT based timed assessments
* HR and Behavioural Questions
				
This was a fun yet another elimination round. There were lots of games to be played etc.
This round was the final for Interview Shortlisting. 

## INTERVIEWS : 
We were told there would be 3 rounds of interviews, all with definite elimination. 

### First Round : Technical
I started off with a technical introduction to the basic question, "Tell me about yourself". Since I had already started to work on my 8th semester major project and included it in my introduction, I was asked 3-4 questions on that.

Then the real interview for the Job started. We started off with an easy SQL question that could be solved with a self-join.
It was immediately followed by a Medium level question which involved usage of Window Functions and some aggregate function like AVG, COUNT etc.

After the queries were done I was asked a question about database performance optimisation. We talked a bit about Sharding. That was the end of Databases and SQL.

The interviewer then asked 2 DSA questions. 
- A simple Sliding Window algorithm based question (dry run + algo).
- Reversing a LinkedList (strictly Python code)

After this quick section we moved to Core ML concepts. I had mentioned relevant projects in the field thus we picked up a few algorithms from there and discussed their significance and working (involved calculus) . They were :
- Softmax function
- Gradient Descent
- ReLu activation function.

From this we moved to some Statistical concepts like :
- Hypothesis testing
- Confidence Intervals 
- Standard Error in Sampling 

Some really tricky questions were asked in this above 3 topics in which were non-intuitive. Good grasp on these basic concepts are enough to crack them.

Overall the technical round was descent. It took time for both me and the interviewer to adjust our paces and vibe. It ended well.

### Managerial Round
This was post lunch. Luckily I was the first person to be sent to the managerial round. I was interviewed by the hiring team manager itself. He stuck to the resume and asked me some basic tech question which were like MCQs. 

**Minor Project :**
We talked about my minor project a lot. It was a reinforcement learning project. We talked about the game logic, policies, reward - penalty fine tuning etc. 
Later we moved to the correlation matrix and Bellman equations. It ended with the manager giving me a particular scenario from the project and asking how that would affect the policy and model's learning.

After that concluded I was asked to explain any ML algorithm like I would to make a 10 grade student understand. I picked up the basic Neural network model with a ReLu activation function to do so. 
I was also asked to explain the Back-Propagation calculus.
This was followed by some naive questions like :
- Choosing learning rate
- Regularisation significance
- Methods of normalisation

I got to use the company's iPad which was fun and lightened my mood a bit. 
This round went better than the previous one.

### HR Round : Final
This round started as soon as I ended my Managerial. (which hinted a possibility at my possible shortlisting)
It started off with some basic questions on my primary and secondary schooling, Parents work and occupation. Then I had to talk about non technical interests etc.
I was given some situation based questions which involved conflict resolution based scenarios. I gave pretty standard answers which were genuine added with a touch of diplomacy.

Post all these I was asked some final questions on relocation and work guidelines. 

### Results :
As I was expecting, I was selected for the role. I was the sole final selection from the 300 initial applicants for the role. The feeling was surreal and I was happy to have gotten the role in this domain. 

It was a good experience overall which really challenged my abilities to understand Math behind ML concepts. 
I have accepted the offer. [6 month Internship + FTE]

Thank you.
Have a great day.

Status: Fresher from Tier-1 college.
**Offer: 6 month + FTE (On-Campus)
Compensation: 45k (6 months stipend), 34L CTC (20 LPA base)**

The hiring process consist of 3 rounds.

**Round-1: Online Assessment**
3 questions were asked in this round. Every student had different set of questions. 35 students shortlisted in this round. 
First two questions were easy-medium, one of sliding window and one of DP (knapsack variation).
Third question was hard. Most probably, it can be solved using meet in the middle.
I had passed all the testcases in first two questions and passed 12/15 testcases in last question.
**Takeaway: Leetcode questions are enough for coding rounds.**

**Round-2: Interview R1 (LLD Round)**
He asked me to design a cab booking application with the functionalities like add driver, add rider, update location, find ride, book ride, calculate bill, etc. They were testing OOPs skills in this round. They were not expecting any kind of use of design patterns here.
**Takeaway: No need to learn LLD design patterns for fresher role. Learn OOPs concepts thoroughly.**

**Round-3: Interview R2 (Hiring Managerial Round)**
This round revolved around each and every line written in the resume. He asked me questions on each and every keyword written in the resume. He also asked some situation based questions. He asked me about my interest then asked questions related to it as well.
**Takeaway: Don't claim anything that you have not done in resume. Give all the answers confidently.**

Only 5 students got selected. And, I was one of them.
If you want the resources from which I have prepared for placements. Let me know in the comments.
